content: Abdominal hair refers to the hair that grows on the human abdomen, located between the pubic region and the thorax (chest). In humans and other mammals, abdominal hair typically grows in a vertical direction, extending upward from the pubic area and downward from the thorax toward the navel. In non-human mammals, this hair is part of their fur or pelage. In humans, the abdominal region is covered with fine, soft vellus hair before puberty. However, during and after puberty, as androgen levels (primarily testosterone) increase, the skin in this area begins to produce coarser, longer, and more pigmented terminal hair. This transformation is more pronounced in males. Initially, the hair forms a vertical line extending from the pubic area to the navel and from the thorax to the navel. While the development of abdominal hair typically begins during puberty, it can also start later, between the ages of 20 and 30. In some men, the abdominal hair remains confined to a distinct vertical line, while in others, the terminal hair spreads laterally around the navel as well as vertically. This lateral spread may continue into middle age. In women, a small line of hair may develop from the pubic area to the navel. In certain cultures, this is considered attractive, while in others, it is viewed as undesirable. When women develop excessive abdominal hair that follows a male pattern, this condition is referred to as hirsutism. Studies have identified four general patterns of pubic and abdominal hair distribution, particularly in Caucasian individuals: 1. Horizontal Pattern: In this pattern, the upper edge of the pubic hair forms a horizontal line, with no hair extending onto the abdomen. 2. Sagittal Pattern: This pattern is similar to the horizontal one but includes a narrow vertical band of hair extending from the pubic region toward the navel. 3. Acuminate Pattern: This pattern is characterized by a tapered, inverted V shape of hair extending upward from the pubic region. The upper limit of this pattern may end below the navel, at the navel, above the navel, or near the chest. 4. Disperse (or Quadrangular) Pattern: In this pattern, hair is distributed broadly across the abdomen without forming a distinct geometric shape. Research by Zickler and others has documented the prevalence of these patterns. The horizontal pattern is the most common in females, occurring in approximately 80% of cases, and is also seen in about 40% of males under the age of 25. The sagittal pattern is observed in about 17% of females and 6% of males. The acuminate pattern is found in about 55% of males and occasionally in females. The disperse pattern is present in approximately 19% of males. For further information, studies such as those by Setty and Zickler provide detailed descriptions and illustrations of these abdominal hair patterns, along with their observed frequencies in different populations.
